subject: Late-hour circuit-breaker activation: urgent safeguard for KV cache memory leak
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Hale <ops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 01:12:00 -0700
Subject: Late-hour circuit-breaker activation: urgent safeguard for KV cache memory leak

Hi Jordan — quick heads up from Redwood Ops.

During a late-night baseline sweep we observed an anomalous growth in KV cache residency on a small subset of Dedicated instances serving your account. The condition is contributing to intermittent OOMs under sustained long-sequence workloads. We are not seeing user data corruption, but there is a measurable increase in error-rate for long requests (p95 latency spikes and a small number of retried requests).

We plan to perform an emergency hotfix: toggle the circuit-breaker to degrade to limited-prefetch mode and apply a short runtime guard that trims oversized KV entries. This reduces memory pressure and preserves latency for short requests. The change is non-destructive and can be reversed. Expected impact: ~2–6 minute maintenance window where a subset of long-running requests may be rate-limited or retried automatically.

Planned window (UTC-7): 01:25–01:35 (10 minutes). This is short-notice — we wanted to notify you before action. Action items we will take: 
- Activate circuit-breaker (immediate)
- Apply KV-trim guard and restart affected worker pool (rolling, no global outage)
- Run smoke suite and open a verification ticket with you

Attachments: runtime-log-sample-20290615.txt (excerpt).

If you need us to delay or to execute a different fallback (full traffic drain to dedicated fallbacks), reply now and cc your on-call. Otherwise we will proceed at 01:25.

Apologies for the short notice — Ben and Karthik are standing by and will provide play-by-play.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Hale <ops@acme-corp.com>

Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 01:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Late-hour circuit-breaker activation: urgent safeguard for KV cache memory leak

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the proactive note.

A few quick questions before you proceed: 
1) Can you confirm there is no risk to persisted customer data and no change to retention?
2) Do you have a rollback plan if the guard causes unexpected latency for our long-batch jobs?
3) Please include our security team on the postmortem.

If the change is reversible and non-destructive, go ahead with the short window. We will put our on-call in monitor mode and watch for alerts.

Jordan Hale
Head of Reliability — Acme Corp
ops@acme-corp.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 01:28:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Late-hour circuit-breaker activation: urgent safeguard for KV cache memory leak

Marissa — forwarding the briefed plan and technical notes so we have a single record.

On Sat, Jun 15, 2029 at 01:12 AM PDT Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> (original message)

Operational plan (short):
- 01:25: flip config.flag.kv_prefetch_mode -> limited-prefetch (runtime flip)
- 01:26: deploy KV-trim guard (binary small patch) to pool-A (rolling 1 host at a time)
- 01:30: verify memory metrics (host-level RSS, heap, and KV-residency) and request p95
- 01:32: run smoke tests against customer canary route (Acme account)
- 01:35: mark DONE if metrics stable, else roll back to previous config by 01:40

Rollback plan: revert config.flag and redeploy previous runtime artifact. We keep the pre-patch image for immediate redeploy; that takes ~2 minutes per host worst-case, so full rollback of the small pool is estimated <10 minutes.

Risks/migration notes: small chance of increased retries for in-flight long requests; we will surface X-Redwood-Retry header when we retry. No disk-level changes, no TTL/retention changes.

Attachments: deploy-instructions.pdf (runbook) attached.

Ben (on-call)
Ben Carter
Incident Response — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Hale <ops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, security@acme-corp.com
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 02:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Late-hour circuit-breaker activation: urgent safeguard for KV cache memory leak — COMPLETE

Jordan — update: we executed the safeguard at 01:25 and completed the rolling apply by 01:34. Summary: 
- Circuit-breaker toggled to limited-prefetch; KV-trim guard applied to pool-A (3 hosts).
- Memory residency returned to baseline within ~4 minutes on all affected hosts. Host RSS and KV-residency charts attached as post-apply-smoke-results.csv.
- Customer-facing impact: brief increase in retries for a small fraction of very long requests (<0.4% of total volume) — automatic retries succeeded. We surfaced X-Redwood-Retry when we retried. No persisted data changes.

Next steps:
- We will open an internal postmortem and share a customer-facing summary within 48 hours.
- Karthik to lead a root-cause analysis around prefetch sizing heuristics and propose a long-term fix (config + telemetry).
- Marissa to schedule a 30-min review with Acme and their security contact for tomorrow 09:30 PT.

If you would like an immediate rollback to previous behavior, tell us now; otherwise we will keep the guard in place while we complete analysis.

Thanks for the quick coordination and apologies again for the late notice.

—Marissa
